name: Chicken Stir Fry
desc: Chicken marinated in a soy, brown sugar and ginger sauce, stir-fried with broccoli, peppers, carrots and water chestnuts over rice.

source.title: Chicken Stir-Fry Recipe
source.evidence: Same sauce (2/3 cup soy sauce, 1/4 cup brown sugar, 1 tbsp cornstarch, 1 tbsp ginger, 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes), 3 chicken breasts, 2 tbsp sesame oil, water chestnuts, broccoli, carrots and onion over 2 cups rice; this version uses a red rather than green bell pepper.

ingredients.raw: 3 boneless skinless chicken breasts (about 1 1/2 lb), cut into bite-size pieces
1 (8 oz) can sliced water chestnuts, drained

steps: Cook the rice: Bring the rice and water to a boil in a saucepan over high heat. Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until tender and the water is absorbed, 20-25 minutes.

Make the marinade: Stir the soy sauce, brown sugar, and cornstarch in a bowl until smooth, then mix in the ginger, garlic, and red pepper flakes. Coat the chicken in it and refrigerate for at least 15 minutes.
Heat 1 tbsp sesame oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Stir-fry the bell pepper, water chestnuts, broccoli, carrots, and onion until crisp-tender, about 5 minutes. Remove to a plate.
Lift the chicken from the marinade, reserving the liquid. Heat the remaining 1 tbsp sesame oil in the skillet over medium-high and cook the chicken about 2 minutes per side, until browned.

Return the vegetables and the reserved marinade to the skillet. Bring to a boil and cook, stirring, until the sauce thickens and the chicken is cooked through (165°F), 5-7 minutes. Serve over the rice.
tips: The marinade is boiled with the chicken for 5 to 7 minutes, which makes it safe to use as the sauce.

references.title: Chicken Stir-Fry Recipe
